parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file passes. src/infrastructure/http.ts is an Express transport adapter. Its work is all infrastructure (transport) work: it builds the app, sets up JSON body parsing, registers routes, checks request shapes (types, non-empty strings, path parameters) and maps errors to HTTP statuses and response bodies. Every business operation goes to the application services (placeOrder, changeState, advance, cancel, listStock, getStock). The check on order states uses the domain's own isOrderState and ORDER_STATES instead of copying their logic. The file does not enforce any business rules itself: it only checks that quantity is a number, not that it is positive, and it decides nothing about stock or state transitions. It has no persistence logic either. Turning domain errors into HTTP status codes is an adapter job, so it belongs here.
